title: Interest Reserve on Operating Lines of Credit with Returned Payments
content:
Where payments on one of the Operating Lines of Credit have come back unpaid in the past year, an interest reserve is held back from what the line will advance.

## Rule

An interest reserve is taken off. It is the outstanding principal multiplied by the line's contract rate in force, read as a percentage:

- **multiplied by 90 and divided by 365** when two or more payments on the line came back unpaid in the twelve whole months before today;
- **multiplied by 30 and divided by 365** when exactly one did;
- **nothing** when none did.

The reserve is rounded to cents. Payments that came back unpaid are the returned interest payments and returned principal payments on the line's transaction history. The contract rate in force is the rate recorded on the line. The reserve is taken off the lending limit together with the outstanding principal.

## Worked figures (hypothetical, outstanding principal USD 300,000.00, contract rate 7.050%)

| Payments returned unpaid in the twelve whole months before today | Interest reserve |
|---|---|
| None | Nothing |
| One | USD 300,000.00 multiplied by 7.050%, by 30 and divided by 365, that is USD 1,738.356…, rounded to USD 1,738.36 |
| Two | USD 300,000.00 multiplied by 7.050%, by 90 and divided by 365, that is USD 5,215.068…, rounded to USD 5,215.07 |
| Four | USD 5,215.07 |
